content.title: A Guide to Vacationing in the Seychelles Islands
content.text: Nestled in the Indian Ocean east of Kenya and north of Madagascar is a 115-island archipelago so beautiful that early British explorers thought they had stumbled upon the Garden of Eden. The Seychelles Islands attract visitors seeking the ultimate romantic vacation or luxurious beach getaway. After all, there are few places more isolated than this heavenly cluster of islands. But there's more to the Seychelles Islands than pristine white sand and water so clear you never lose sight of your feet. In addition to abundant natural beauty and wildlife, the largest island, Mahé, is home to beautiful 18th- and 19th-century French and British architecture in the capital city of Victoria. And that's to say nothing of the incredible seafood and resorts. As you prepare to book a full day of flights to reach this island paradise, check out our definitive guide to planning the perfect Seychelles getaway. What to Know Seychelles Islands, Mahe Island secret beach. Getty Images The Seychelles Islands are not known to have been inhabited until the French began colonizing the area in the 1770s. Over the years, the islands passed between the British and French before gaining independence from Britain in 1976. Today, these multicultural islands make up a sovereign republic within the Commonwealth of Nations. Most Seychellois trace their roots back to early French settlers and East Africans who arrived later. There is also a considerable South Indian and Chinese influence, which you'll notice in the islands' seafood-heavy cuisine. If you're a United States passport holder, you don't need a visa, but you must obtain an electronic travel authorization from the Seychelles government up to 30 days before your flight. You'll need to show proof of return transportation, accommodations, and sufficient funds for the duration of the trip. What to Pack The Seychelles Islands have a tropical rain forest climate with substantial humidity that's tempered by cool ocean breezes. Pack plenty of swimwear, loose-fitting clothes, and open-toe footwear, as much of your time here will be spent on the beach. Hiking is also a popular activity, so consider bringing some sturdy boots. Keep in mind that the rainy season runs from December through February. What to See Getty Images / iStockphoto Beaches are the main draw in this island nation, and since the archipelago is so far-flung, many are virtually untouched. The island of La Digue is known for Anse Source d’Argent beach, one of Africa's most beautiful beaches, with a shoreline framed by picturesque granite boulders. On the island of Praslin, Anse Lazio beach is famous for its clear blue waters and native takamaka trees. Inland, visitors can explore the Vallée de Mai Nature Preserve, a UNESCO World Heritage site. This dense jungle is home to primitive plant and animal species that have remained isolated since the islands were formed. If you're lucky, you may catch a glimpse of the Seychelles black parrot, found nowhere else on the planet. When you need a break from sun and sand, visit the Seychelles' capital city, Victoria. Located on Mahé, which is home to the majority of the population, it has incredible architecture, open-air markets, museums, and a vibrant nightlife scene. Where to Stay Courtesy of Fregate Island Resort While budget-friendly lodging is available, splurge-worthy resorts are major draws. The Waldorf Astoria Seychelles, which opened on Platte Island in 2024, offers 50 private villas and its own beach and lagoon. On the private island of Félicité, you can stay in one of 30 ocean-facing villas at Six Senses Zil Pasyon, where you'll get your own plunge pool, and on Petite Anse, there's the luxe Four Seasons Resort Seychelles, complete with an open-air spa and breathtaking views. To really immerse yourself in nature and feel the stark isolation of the Seychelles, consider staying in one of the 11 thatched-roof beachfront villas on North Island. How to Get There The Seychelles Islands are between 500 and 1,000 miles off the coast of mainland Africa, so the best way to reach them is by plane. Most connecting flights originate from Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. Travel between the islands is typically by small plane or helicopter. Ferry service between the main islands of Mahé, La Digue, and Praslin is operated by Seychellesbookings.com.
